summary:
Osun State stands under Nigeria's national criminal framework, and the Same-Sex Marriage (Prohibition) Act 2014 applies in Osun as in every other state, reaching visitors and non-citizens as well as residents. The UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office travel advisory of 19 August 2026 warns LGBT+ travellers to Nigeria of arrest, violence, attacks, blackmail and intimidation, stating that same-sex sexual activity is illegal and can attract up to 14 years' imprisonment, with the law also reaching wedding arrangers and organisers and anyone involved with gay groups. Those federal penalties and arrest-risk warnings apply in full in Osun.

The advisory's death-penalty warning under Sharia law applies only to Nigeria's northern states and does not apply in Osun, where the federal penalties are the operative exposure.

Osun sits within a national climate in which mass arrests and detention of LGBTQ+ people are common, especially in northern states, despite constitutional guarantees of non-discrimination and of private and family life. The killing of the transgender TikToker 'Abuja Area Mama', whose beaten body was found along the Katampe–Mabushi expressway in Abuja on 9 August 2024, roughly a year after she had said she feared for her life, illustrates the lethal violence and subsequent impunity that trans Nigerians face; an investigation was announced, and no charges had been brought six months later.
tangentialFactors:
Enforcement patterns elsewhere in Nigeria indicate the forms of exposure a trans visitor in Osun could encounter: mass arrests at social venues, including 100-plus party-goers at a hotel in Asaba in June 2018, 57 young men at Egbeda, Lagos, in August 2018, the 'Warri 67' in August 2023, and 76 people at a party in Gombe in October 2023. These are raw counts from a national tally, not per-capita rates, and they do not measure Osun specifically.

Police elsewhere have used the statute against people for how they appear: a 24-year-old man was struck by Lagos police in March 2025 for 'looking gay' and released only after paying part of a demanded bribe. Dating applications carry documented entrapment risk through 'kito' gangs that lure LGBTQ+ Nigerians to meetings where they are beaten, filmed and blackmailed.
localsOnly:
Residents of Osun live under the federal SSMPA regime and the national pattern of police extortion, arbitrary arrest and hostility documented across Nigeria. LGBTQ Nigerians nationally report fearing medical care and crime reporting, and activists say the Act hampers access to HIV prevention services; the same chilling effect reaches Osun's residents and community health workers.

Placement and custody questions for trans Nigerians remain discretionary: Bobrisky (Idris Okuneye) was held in Kirikiri maximum-security prison after an April 2024 sentence, and an October 2024 panel found that placement violated the Nigerian Correctional Service Act because she was a first-time offender.
outOfScopeNotes:
No Osun-specific enforcement incident, arrest, state house of assembly bill or local judicial decision was identified in the source inventory; the assessment rests on the national framework and national-climate evidence. Whether Osun State police have conducted venue raids or applied the SSMPA within the state is not sourced here.

The advisory's applicability to cross-dressing proposals reported in September 2022, and any Osun-specific facilities or care-access practice, remain unresolved in these sources.
